todays_goal: Advance reflection into how flat mirrors create virtual images.

lessons.subject: science
lessons.lesson_title: How a Mirror Makes an Image
lessons.previous_learning: Day 20 showed strong understanding of the normal line, equal incidence/reflection angles, and periscope reflection.
lessons.course_context: Use reflected rays to explain why a flat-mirror image appears behind the mirror.
learning_objectives: Explain why the brain locates a virtual image behind a mirror.
Use equal object-image distance for a flat mirror.
lessons.why_it_matters: Ray models explain what mirrors show and connect reflection to real optical systems.

vocabulary.definition: an image that appears where light rays do not actually meet
a backward dotted line showing where reflected light seems to come from

lessons.written_instruction: Atticus: actual light travels object -> mirror -> eye. Your brain traces the reflected rays backward, so the image appears behind the mirror.

worked_examples.title: Behind the mirror
worked_examples.problem: Why does a mirror image look behind the glass?
worked_examples.solution: The brain traces reflected rays backward.
worked_examples.explanation: The rays do not actually travel from behind the mirror.

worked_examples.title: Equal distance
worked_examples.problem: Object is 30 cm in front of a flat mirror.
worked_examples.solution: Image appears about 30 cm behind it.
worked_examples.explanation: Flat mirrors place the virtual image the same distance behind as the object is in front.

independent_practice.prompt: What is the actual light path when you see yourself in a mirror?
Why does the image seem to be behind the mirror?
Object is 20 cm in front of mirror. Where does image appear?
Draw object -> mirror -> eye and backward dotted ray extensions.

exit_ticket.prompt: Why does a mirror image appear behind the mirror?
exit_ticket.answer: The brain traces reflected rays backward as if they came from behind the mirror.

exit_ticket.prompt: You stand 1 m in front of a flat mirror. About how far behind the mirror does the image appear?

lessons.voice_prompt: Teach with an actual-path versus apparent-path drawing on the whiteboard. Use solid lines for real reflected rays and dotted backward extensions for the virtual image. Use a different object distance from Atticus's assigned work. Do not draw his final diagram.
